title: Lower airfares seen
summary: Filipinos planning a trip for the Christmas holiday will get a slight relief in airfares, as the Civil Aeronautics Board has lowered the fuel surcharge by a notch until end-November.

blocks.text: Stock photo of individuals waiting for their flight.

MANILA, Philippines — Filipinos planning a trip for the Christmas holiday will get a slight relief in airfares, as the Civil Aeronautics Board (CAB) has lowered the fuel surcharge by a notch until end-November.
In an advisory, CAB said it is cutting the fuel surcharge to Level 16 for Nov. 16 to 30, from Level 17 formerly.
At Level 16, airlines can impose a fuel surcharge of P525 to P1,535 for domestic flights and a pass-on fee of P1,733.76 to P12,891.29 for international trips.
Filipinos headed for Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand have to pay P2,397.82 more under Level 16 while those headed to Indonesia, Japan and South Korea will have pay a fuel surcharge of P2,697.07.
The highest fuel surcharge will be slapped on travelers taking transpacific trips, hitting P7,530.97 for flights to Honolulu and P12,277.42 for departures to North America.
Locally, the highest fuel surcharge will be felt on Manila flights to General Santos at P1,535.
Manila trips to Cotabato, Davao and Zamboanga are accorded the second highest fuel surcharge among domestic destinations at P1,431.

CAB said airlines wishing to collect the fuel surcharge must submit an application to the agency. It also asked carriers transacting in foreign currencies to observe an exchange rate of P63.61 to $1 in collecting their fuel surcharge.
Based on the monitor of the International Air Transport Association, jet fuel prices have dropped by 12 percent on a monthly basis to $169.82 per barrel as of Sept. 18.
However, prices will continue to fluctuate due to the Middle East conflict.
For Filipinos, the slight reduction in fares opens a window for them to book flights, as they also deal with a weak peso that has made it costlier to travel internationally.
Historically, November marks the peak of the booking season for air travel, as Filipinos plan the trips that they would make on the Christmas and New Year holidays.
